title: CodyScript program
description: A program is an input: a literal or an input node, usually a block ({ "do": [...] }). Its root node may also define CodyScript functions ("fn"), declare the external functions the host provides ("ext"), declare types ("types") and carry tests ("tests"); "call" calls either kind of function, "is" and "problems" check a value against a type, and "expect" fails a run unless a value holds. Every node is an object whose type is its key. The engine's compile() also checks what each call and type names, that no name is in both "fn" and "ext", that only external calls take "arg", that the host provides every "ext" function, that no type is only itself, that only tests "run" the program, nesting depth and finite numbers.

literal.description: A bare number, string, boolean or null is its own value. A string is text, never a variable.

node.description: An input node: exactly one of its types, each defined with the fields it may carry (closed where it's used: an input takes no others, the root also "fn", "ext", "types" and "tests").

tag.description: An opaque label echoed back in errors.

functions.description: The program's own functions, by name: each a program of its own, whose only variables are its arguments. Names may contain dots ("text.size"), but none may also be in "ext". Only the root may carry it.

externals.description: The external functions the program may call, by executor: { "text": ["trim", "empty"] } declares text.trim and text.empty. The host must provide each. Only the root may carry it.

types.description: The types the program declares, by name: each a type, which may name others, and itself (inside an object, list or map). A name can't end with "?", nor be a built-in type's. Only the root may carry it.

type.description: A type: a name — a built-in (any, null, boolean, number, integer, string, list, object) or one the program declares in "types" — and with "?" after it, or null (an object's field may then be left out); or an object, list or map of types.

typeNode.description: { "obj": { <field>: <type>, … } }: an object with these fields and no others. { "list": <type> }: a list of them. { "map": <type> }: an object whose every field's value is one.

tests.description: The program's tests, by name: each a program of its own, which passes if it runs to the end. It may call the program's functions and the host's, and "run" the program. Only the root may carry it.

val.description: A constant of any type; nothing inside it is read as a node. Only needed for objects and arrays.

x.description: An expression over variables: numbers, 'text', true, false, null, names, fields and items (a.b, a[0], a['b'], and a?.b, a?[0] for ones that may be missing), + - * /, parentheses, one comparison (== != < <= > >=), && || and ! (on booleans), and ?? (a default for null). Syntax is checked by compile().

call.description: Calls a function: one key, its name — one the program defines in "fn" or declares in "ext" — whose value names the arguments to compute.

additionalProperties.description: Arguments, resolved in order. A CodyScript function's are its variables.

arg.description: A static argument, passed as written. Only for external functions.

block.description: Runs instructions in a new scope; its value is what it returns, else null.

obj.description: Builds an object: each field's value is an input, resolved in order. (For a constant object, use val.)

list.description: Builds a list: each item is an input, resolved in order. (For a constant list, use val.)

is.description: Whether a value is a type: true or false.

problems.description: What's wrong with a value as a type: a list of { path, message }, empty if it is one.

run.description: In a test, runs the program with these variables (and no others), and gives its value. compile() checks that only tests run it.

set.description: Assigns one variable in the current scope: { "set": { "<name>": <input> } }.

ret.description: Ends the enclosing block with a value.

if.description: Runs do when the test is true, otherwise el. The test must be a boolean.

for.description: Runs do while the test is true. The test must be a boolean.

expect.description: Fails the run (and a test) with expectation_failed unless the value is true — or, with eq, equal to eq's: lists item by item, objects field by field in any order, numbers by value.
